sources.quote: Bill 96, passed in 2022, amended Quebec's Charter of the French Language
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Loi sur la langue officielle et commune du Québec, le français
sources.evidence: The Law on the official and common language of Quebec, French (Bill 96) was sanctioned on June 1, 2022. It was on this date that the majority of amendments to the Charter of the French Language came into force. The new law led notably to the creation of the Ministry of the French Language, the appointment of the first commissioner for the French language, and a strengthening of the required obligations.

sources.quote: Commercial publications aimed at the Quebec market must be available in French
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Médias sociaux, sites Web et documents publicitaires
sources.evidence: Commercial publications must be written in French, including those distributed on websites and social media. Commercial publications can be written in two distinct versions, provided that the French version is available under conditions of accessibility and quality at least equal to the version written in another language.

sources.quote: It must offer French on terms at least as favourable as any other language
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Charte de la langue française - Changements législatifs (FAQ: sites Web et médias sociaux)
sources.evidence: When the law requires French, the use of one or more other languages is permitted if French appears in at least equivalent fashion, which means the same information must be offered in French and in any other language. The rules provided by the Charter of the French Language apply, with necessary adaptations, to content conveyed by the Internet. Commercial advertising found on companies' web pages must have a French version unless it is covered by one of the exceptions provided in the regulation.

sources.quote: a recognized trademark in another language can appear, but French descriptive text must appear alongside it on signage and must be markedly predominant
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Entreprises : affichage des marques de commerce et des noms d'entreprises
sources.evidence: New rules concerning public signage and commercial advertising, notably regarding business names or trademarks, have been in effect since June 1, 2025. A recognized trademark that is entirely or partially in a language other than French and appears in signage visible from outside a building must be accompanied by terms in French – such as a generic term, a descriptive term or a slogan – to ensure clear predominance of French. The French text must occupy a space at least twice as large as text in another language.

sources.quote: Standard-form contracts and related documents must be presented in French first; the customer may then expressly choose another language
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Entreprises : contrats d'adhésion
sources.evidence: Since June 1, 2023, every new contract of adhesion must first be provided in French to the person adhering. After the provision of the French version, the parties can choose to conclude the contract in another language than French if such is their express will. The documents connected to the contract can then be drafted solely in that other language.

sources.quote: the threshold for mandatory OQLF registration and francization fell from 50 to
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Démarche de francisation : Les entreprises employant de 25 à 49 personnes sont invitées à s'inscrire à l'Office québécois de la langue française sans attendre
sources.evidence: À compter du 1er juin 2025, l'obligation de s'inscrire à l'Office québécois de la langue française afin d'entreprendre une démarche de francisation s'étend aux entreprises de 25 à 49 personnes. Les entreprises qui emploient au Québec 25 personnes ou plus durant une période de 6 mois ont l'obligation de s'inscrire à l'Office afin d'entamer une démarche de francisation.

sources.quote: doubled on a second offence and tripled thereafter
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Vivre en français - Entreprises - Infractions et peines
sources.evidence: L'auteur du manquement est passible d'une amende de 700 $ à 7 000 $ dans le cas d'une personne physique et de 3 000 $ à 30 000 $ dans le cas d'une personne morale. Toute récidive entraîne une amende plus lourde, soit le double pour une première récidive et le triple pour toute récidive additionnelle.

sources.quote: Customers have the right to be served in French
sources.publisher: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
sources.title: Langue du commerce et des affaires - vos droits en tant que consommateur ou consommatrice
sources.evidence: The customers of businesses operating in Quebec have the right to be served and informed in French, whether before, during, or after a transaction. Every business conducting activities in Quebec must offer services and products in French, regardless of the type of business. Commercial publications of businesses operating in Quebec must be written in French.

sources.quote: Proper hreflang tags (fr-CA and en-CA) so Google serves the right version to the right searcher
sources.title: Localized Versions of your Pages | Google Search Central | Documentation | Google for Developers
sources.evidence: Use hreflang to tell Google about the variations of your content, so that Google can understand that these pages are localized variations of the same content. The value of the hreflang attribute identifies the language (in ISO 639-1 format) and optionally a region (in ISO 3166-1 Alpha 2 format) of an alternate URL. If page X links to page Y, page Y must link back to page X.
